desc: baseline
[real] Reduce learning_rate to 0.1 and increase n_estimators to 200 for better generalization
reflection: This is the first experiment, so there's no prior trajectory to analyze. The baseline is an untuned XGBClassifier with library defaults. For spambase (a spam classification task with ~4600 samples, 57 features, 2 classes), the most impactful first changes are typically: (1) tuning learning_rate and n_estimators, (2) adjusting tree depth/complexity, or (3) adding regularization. I'll start with a standard approach: reduce learning_rate and increase n_estimators, which often helps XGBoost generalize better than the defaults.

desc: [real] Increase max_depth to 8 to capture more complex feature interactions

The previous attempt (#001) tried reducing learning_rate to 0.1 and increasing n_estimators to 200, but it was discarded with val=0.0478 (worse than baseline). This suggests the default learning_rate=0.3 might actually be better for this dataset, or the increased n_estimators wasn't sufficient to compensate. I'll try a different approach: increasing max_depth from the default 6 to allow more complex trees, which often helps on high-dimensional tabular data like spambase (57 features).
